source.title: Generalization and Estimation Error Bounds for Model-based Neural Networks
source.authors: Avner Shultzman; Eyar Azar; M. Rodrigues; Yonina C. Eldar

record.file_problem: none; full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: Reports empirical comparisons of model-based ISTA and ReLU networks on estimation error, a different measure and task from the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper also derives theoretical bounds and discusses cited findings about generalization, but those are not empirical results on the listed versions. The empirical comparisons below are reported in text; precise plotted values are not stated.
record.test_reason: The study derives conditional error bounds and compares ISTA with ReLU networks on simulated sparse recovery. Neither its experiments nor its theoretical arguments test V1–V8. A different task and measure alone do not qualify it as T2.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate when restricted to conditional bounds. The authors derive GE and EE bounds for ISTA and ADMM and conditions for a nonincreasing GE bound with depth. Experiments evaluate ISTA versus ReLU, finding lower small-sample empirical EE and recovery loss and sensitivity to the soft threshold. Lower EE does not necessarily imply lower recovery loss. Comparing upper bounds alone does not establish the ordering of actual errors.
record.recipe_differences: Model-based sparse-recovery networks versus ReLU feed-forward networks; simulated inverse-problem data and estimation error rather than the claim versions' classification, language, memorization, sharpness, or example-removal tests.
record.method_sensitivity: Training sample count and soft-threshold value affect the reported estimation-error comparison; bias choice is described as less significant than nonlinearity choice.

fits_no_version.finding: ISTA has lower empirical estimation error and L1 recovery loss than ReLU with few training samples; empirical estimation errors approach zero relative to each architecture's large-sample reference.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Soft-threshold ISTA networks can improve sparse recovery and sample efficiency relative to the tested ReLU networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing the soft threshold reduces small-sample estimation error, but lower estimation error need not yield lower recovery loss; threshold sensitivity fades with more samples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The soft threshold controls empirical estimation error in the tested ISTA networks, with a possible tradeoff in recovery loss.

fits_no_version.finding: Constant versus learned biases influence estimation error and recovery performance less than the choice of nonlinearity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Nonlinearity matters more than bias learning in the tested sparse-recovery comparisons.

record.problems: Empirical results are limited to simulated sparse vector recovery and use an empirical approximation to the ERM and optimal estimator. Precise figure values and uncertainty estimates are not stated in the text. The theoretical comparisons rely on stated assumptions and bounds, not direct measurement of the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out natural-label versus random-label accuracy.
Width increases beyond zero training error and their effect on test error; depth bounds do not test this.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classification, local connectivity, and initialization effects.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and the effects of tuning or optimizer modifications.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects and interactions with dataset size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparison with other measures.
Removing memorized versus random training examples and measuring test accuracy after retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8; this does not reject the reported sparse-recovery findings. GE is a class-level quantity and empirical EE is excess population loss over an approximated architecture-specific optimum, rather than a measured training–test gap. Supplementary depth experiments and convolutional extensions do not test the listed width or architectural-comparison claims.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train these architectures on fixed random labels or compare their held-out accuracy with natural-label training.
Does not sweep network width beyond the interpolation threshold.
Compares ISTA and ReLU networks on sparse vector recovery, not convolutional and fully connected image classifiers or local connectivity.
Uses SGD; does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD on image or language benchmarks.
Does not vary batch size or compare large and small batches.
Does not test dropout or its interaction with weight decay and data augmentation.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare sharpness with other gap measures.
Does not remove memorized training examples or measure their effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: ISTA network
rows.operation_detail: Compared empirical estimation error against a ReLU network across training-set sizes.

conditions.value: small number; between 10 and 10^4 samples tested

rows.baseline: ReLU network; exact value not stated
rows.value: For a small number of training samples, ISTA substantially reduces estimation error compared to ReLU; exact value not stated.
rows.note: The text describes the comparison; numerical values are shown only in the figure.
rows.check: The reported small-sample estimation-error advantage is supported by Section 5, but measures none of V1–V8.

rows.subject: ISTA network
rows.operation_detail: Compared empirical estimation error against a ReLU network across training-set sizes.
rows.baseline: ReLU network; exact value not stated
rows.value: For large numbers of samples, estimation error of both networks decreases to zero; exact value not stated.
rows.note: The text describes the trend; precise values are not stated.
rows.check: Measures none of V1–V8. The reference estimator is trained on 10^4 samples, so zero empirical estimation error at that endpoint follows from the reference construction; it does not establish zero test loss or zero training–test gap.

rows.subject: ISTA network
rows.operation_detail: Measured empirical estimation error and L1 loss for multiple soft-threshold values.
rows.measure: Empirical estimation error as a function of λ.
rows.value: Increasing λ reduces estimation error; exact values not stated.
rows.note: Authors state the trend in text; plotted values are not transcribed.
rows.check: Soft-threshold sensitivity measures none of V1–V8. The text associates the approximately 100-sample condition with reduced estimation error, and explicitly warns that lower estimation error need not mean lower loss.

rows.subject: ISTA network
rows.operation_detail: Measured empirical estimation error for multiple soft-threshold values.

conditions.value: large number; exact threshold not stated

rows.measure: Empirical estimation error as a function of λ.
rows.value: The dependency on λ vanishes for a large number of training samples; estimation error is similar for all tested λ values.
rows.note: The text states the similarity but does not give plotted values.
rows.check: The reported disappearance of soft-threshold sensitivity at large sample counts concerns estimation error, not any listed version.

rows.subject: ISTA network with constant biases
rows.operation_detail: Compared empirical estimation error and accuracy with the learned-bias variant.
rows.measure: Empirical estimation error and accuracy relative to learned-bias variant.
rows.baseline: ISTA network with learned biases; exact values not stated
rows.value: Bias choice is less significant to estimation error or accuracy than nonlinearity choice; exact values not stated.
rows.note: The authors describe bias choice as less significant; values are not stated.
rows.check: Measures none of V1–V8. Less influence than nonlinearity does not establish a partial directional effect of constant biases. Split estimation error and L1 recovery loss if retaining separate measures; accuracy here is not classification accuracy.

rows.subject: ISTA network with learned biases
rows.operation_detail: Compared empirical estimation error and accuracy with the constant-bias variant.
rows.measure: Empirical estimation error and accuracy relative to constant-bias variant.
rows.baseline: ISTA network with constant biases; exact values not stated
rows.value: Bias choice is less significant to estimation error or accuracy than nonlinearity choice; exact values not stated.
rows.note: The authors describe bias choice as less significant; values are not stated.
rows.check: Duplicates R5's qualitative comparison with the baseline reversed, without an independently stated directional result. Merge with R5; the text does not justify a partial effect.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
